candidates.title: What happens to frameworks in the agents era? to component libraries? to @shadcn? The answer is: we need to drill deeper. Delete the part, optimize, accelerate, automate. UI SDK is like the x86 instruction set for agents to build new UI components spontaneously. Agents are the new design engineers, and they're ready to build *anything* you ask, tailored to your usecase. High-level, rigid, single-framework abstractions are like kryptonite for what is essentially an infinite, untiring creation machine. I think we've found someone that allows us to have the cake and eat it too. A decades-long dream. UI SDK is packaged behaviors that give us accessibility, performance, cohesion, saving us tokens, errors and effort, but with absolutely zero limitations and tradeoffs for what UIs we can generate. Enjoy!

candidates.title: Ok this is a big deal. We’ve been testing Gemini 4 Hydrogen in early access with the Box AI Complex Work Eval, and it’s a serious jump for fast models. Hydrogen is 5 percentage points better in accuracy than Gemini 3.8 Flash. That alone would be a great boost in capability, but possibly more importantly it did the tasks in less than half the time with about 12% fewer tokens on a typical task. For this eval, we give the Box Agent Hydrogen as a model for a series of complex tasks that represent real world work with enterprise documents across finance, consulting, life sciences, and other industries. Hydrogen will be a great model for a lot of efficient but complex tasks across these fields. Gemini team is definitely cooking. Hydrogen will be rolling out in the Box AI Studio shortly so any customer can build a custom agent with it.
